abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains an aggressive, lethal form of cancer and available immunotherapies are ineffective for most patients. In this study, we investigated combining agonistic anti-CD40 (aCD40) with TAK-981 (TAK/subasumstat), a SUMOylation inhibitor with immune priming effects. We previously reported that TAK-981 increases CD40 expression on antigen-presenting cells, and thus we hypothesized that combining it with an agonistic CD40 antibody (aCD40) would enhance immune-mediated tumor control. We investigated the therapeutic effect of TAK-981 + aCD40 in vivo using three syngeneic, orthotopic mouse models of PDAC. Single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence/immunohistochemistry were used to identify immunogenic changes in the tumor microenvironment. T-cell and macrophage depletions were used to assess functional contributions of individual immune cell populations. We assessed the functional contributions of T-cells and macrophages by depleting their populations separately.TAK-981+aCD40 treatment augmented CD8+ T-cell and macrophage infiltration into the tumor, amplified IFNα and IFNγ signaling, decreased TGFβ signaling and increased MHC-I expression resulting in decreased tumor burden and improved median survival. Despite the induction of dramatic CD8+ T cell infiltration into tumors, the efficacy of combination therapy was not impacted by T cell deficiency or depletion. In contrast, depletion of phagocytic macrophages abolished the therapeutic benefit of combination therapy. Therefore, TAK-981+aCD40 combination therapy activates macrophage mediated anti-tumor immunity in the PDAC models. Our findings support further exploration of this combination in clinical trials to validate this combination as a strategy to generate meaningful macrophage-mediated anti-tumor immune responses in pancreatic cancer patients.
key_points_ko: TAK-981과 항-CD40 작용제 병용 치료는 마우스 췌관선암(PDAC) 모델에서 종양 부담을 감소시키고 중앙 생존기간을 향상시켰습니다.
병용 치료는 종양 내 CD8+ T세포와 대식세포 침투를 증가시키고, IFNα 및 IFNγ 신호를 증폭시켰습니다.
대식세포를 고갈시켰을 때는 병용 치료의 치료적 이점이 완전히 사라졌습니다.
summary_ko: 이 연구는 췌관선암(PDAC) 마우스 모델에서 SUMOylation(SUMO화) 억제제인 TAK-981(subasumstat)과 면역 조절 효과가 있는 항-CD40 작용제(aCD40)의 병용 치료 효과를 조사했습니다. 연구 결과, 두 약물의 병용 투여는 종양 내 CD8+ T세포와 대식세포(macrophage)의 침투를 증가시키고 인터페론 신호를 강화하여 종양 부담을 줄이고 중앙 생존기간(median survival)을 향상시켰습니다. T세포 결핍이나 고갈에도 병용 치료의 효과는 유지되었으나, 식세포성 대식세포가 고갈될 경우 치료 효과는 완전히 사라졌습니다. 본 연구는 이 병용요법이 대식세포 매개 항종양 면역 반응을 유발함을 보여주며, 임상시험을 통한 추가 검증을 지지합니다.
title: Targeting SUMOylation in Combination with Agonistic Anti-CD40 Therapy Activates Anti- Tumor Immunity to Control Pancreatic Cancer
title_ko: SUMO화 억제제와 항-CD40 작용제 병용요법을 통한 췌장암 항종양 면역 활성화
